get_random_species.description: Pick a marine species at random, for a species of the day or a quiz, optionally from those matching the same filters as List species, and only from those with a photo if asked. Returns everything recorded about it, as Get a species does. Fails if no species matches.

species.full_description: Hydrophis cyanocinctus reaches 2.75 m. Large sea snake (Elapidae) Indo-Pacific and Persian Gulf with cylindrical body yellow-green to olive-yellow with distinct black-blue to black rings over entire length (hence cyanocinctus, blue-girded), thin head, vertically flattened tail. Lives from 0 to 50 m on coral reefs, sandy bottoms and coastal waters, fully aquatic unlike Laticauda (never leaves water, viviparous). Predator of fish extracted from holes. Powerful venom. Middle East, India, Malaysia dive photo subject, impressive encounter but curious swimmer rather than aggressive.
species.short_description: Large Indo-Pacific yellow-green sea snake with blue rings, fully aquatic, venomous.

Lives from 0 to 50 m on coral reefs, sandy bottoms and coastal waters, fully aquatic unlike Laticauda (never leaves water, viviparous). Predator of fish extracted from holes. Powerful venom. translations.short_description: Large Indo-Pacific yellow-green sea snake with blue rings, fully aquatic, venomous.

translations.full_description: Hydrophis cyanocinctus atteint 2.75 m. Grand serpent marin (Elapidae) Indo-Pacifique et golfe Persique au corps cylindrique jaune-vert à jaune-olive avec anneaux bleu-noir à noir distincts sur toute la longueur (d'où cyanocinctus, ceint de bleu), tête fine, queue aplatie verticalement. Vit de 0 à 50 m sur récifs coralliens, fonds sableux et eaux côtières, totalement aquatique contrairement à Laticauda (ne sort jamais de l'eau, vivipare). Prédateur de poissons qu'il extrait des trous. Venin puissant. Sujet photo plongée Moyen-Orient, Inde, Malaisie, rencontre impressionnante mais nageur curieux plutôt qu'agressif.
translations.short_description: Grand serpent marin Indo-Pacifique jaune-vert à anneaux bleus, totalement aquatique, venimeux.

translations.full_description: Hydrophis cyanocinctus alcanza 2.75 m. Gran serpiente marina (Elapidae) Indo-Pacífica y Golfo Pérsico con cuerpo cilíndrico amarillo-verde a amarillo-oliva con anillos azul-negros a negros distintos en toda la longitud (de ahí cyanocinctus, ceñida de azul), cabeza fina, cola aplanada verticalmente. Vive de 0 a 50 m en arrecifes coralinos, fondos arenosos y aguas costeras, totalmente acuática a diferencia de Laticauda (nunca sale del agua, vivípara). Depredadora de peces que extrae de agujeros. Veneno poderoso. Sujeto fotográfico del Medio Oriente, India, Malasia, encuentro impresionante pero nadadora curiosa más que agresiva.
translations.short_description: Gran serpiente marina Indo-Pacífico amarillo-verde con anillos azules, totalmente acuática, venenosa.

get_species.description: Get everything speCies.blue records about one marine species, by common or scientific name, WoRMS AphiaID or ID: its names and descriptions, photos with their credits, IUCN status, danger to divers, size and depth, habitats, the ocean zones it lives in and its taxonomy. A common name several species share fails, naming them.

species.full_description: Manta birostris (synonym Mobula birostris) reaches 7 m wingspan and 2 tons, the largest ray in the world. Black back with white T-shaped markings on shoulders, white belly with individual black spots allowing photo-ID identification. Two fleshy deployable cephalic fins forming funnel to filter plankton. Circumtropical and subtropical pelagic distribution, famous aggregations at Socorro (Mexico), Galapagos, Maldives, Mozambique (Tofo), Cape Verde. IUCN Endangered. Trophy dive photo subject, moving encounter with these peaceful giants.
species.short_description: Largest ray in the world (7 m wingspan), iconic pelagic of tropical seamounts, IUCN Endangered.

translations.full_description: Manta birostris (synonym Mobula birostris) reaches 7 m wingspan and 2 tons, the largest ray in the world. Circumtropical and subtropical pelagic distribution, famous aggregations at Socorro (Mexico), Galapagos, Maldives, Mozambique (Tofo), Cape Verde. IUCN Endangered. translations.full_description: Manta birostris (synonyme Mobula birostris) atteint 7 m d'envergure et 2 tonnes, la plus grande raie au monde. Dos noir avec marques blanches en T sur les épaules, ventre blanc avec taches noires individuelles permettant l'identification par photo-ID. Deux nageoires céphaliques charnues déployables formant entonnoir pour filtrer le plancton. Distribution circumtropicale et subtropicale pélagique, agrégations célèbres à Socorro (Mexique), Galápagos, Maldives, Mozambique (Tofo), Cap-Vert. Classée En Danger UICN. Sujet photo plongée trophée, rencontre émouvante avec ces géants paisibles.
translations.short_description: Plus grande raie au monde (7 m d'envergure), pélagique iconique des seamounts tropicaux, En Danger UICN.

translations.full_description: Manta birostris (sinónimo Mobula birostris) alcanza 7 m de envergadura y 2 toneladas, la mayor raya del mundo. Dorso negro con marcas blancas en T en hombros, vientre blanco con manchas negras individuales que permiten identificación por foto-ID. Dos aletas cefálicas carnosas desplegables formando embudo para filtrar plancton. Distribución circumtropical y subtropical pelágica, agregaciones famosas en Socorro (México), Galápagos, Maldivas, Mozambique (Tofo), Cabo Verde. Clasificada En Peligro UICN. Sujeto fotográfico trofeo, encuentro emotivo con estos gigantes pacíficos.
translations.short_description: Mayor raya del mundo (7 m de envergadura), pelágica icónica de montes submarinos tropicales, En Peligro UICN.

url.description: Its page on speCies.blue, in the language asked for.

description: Look up marine life in speCies.blue, the field guide for scuba divers: more than 1,500 species of fish, corals, molluscs, crustaceans, sea turtles, marine mammals and more, from the Mediterranean and the Caribbean to the Red Sea and the Asian Pacific. Each comes with its common names and descriptions in English, French and Spanish, photos with their credits, IUCN conservation status, danger to divers, size and depth ranges, habitats, behaviours and taxonomy. Search by name, list and filter by category, status, danger, zone, size or depth, pick one at random, and list the categories and ocean zones. Works without an API key at speCies.blue's anonymous limit of 100 requests a minute, shared across Lodol; add a key for 1,000 a minute of your own.
